summary: Generic crystalline derived monodromy for decent acceptable pairs of an arbitrary connected reductive group over Q_p (GLX26 Theorem 5.8), the finite-extension open-image period point (Proposition 5.9), Zariski density of open subgroups, central lifting and the z-extension comparison, and stabilizers of components of compact-image period torsors. Generic filtrations use the corrected threshold min over the whole Galois orbit, valid for nonnormal reflex fields. The quasisplit converse (Proposition 5.11) and the component theorem (Theorem 6.1) are downstream consumers, not targets.

gaps.needs: For a quasisplit connected reductive group G over a field k of characteristic zero, with a k-Borel B ⊇ T and the Galois action on the dominant weights X*(T)^+, prove that the irreducible k-representations are the W_O for the Γ_k-orbits O of dominant weights, with W_O ⊗ k̄ ≅ ⊕_{λ∈O} W_λ, and that the W_O-isotypic part V_O of every representation satisfies V_O ⊗ k̄ = ⊕_{λ∈O} V^λ_{k̄}, γ(V^λ_{k̄}) = V^{γλ}_{k̄} for γ ∈ Γ_k, and V_O = (⊕_{λ∈O} V^λ_{k̄})^{Γ_k}.

ReductiveGroups Layer 10B treats split groups and Layer 7 the absolute root datum with Galois action; the quasisplit Galois-orbit classification is the extension requested. The generic filtration, the threshold formula and Frobenius transport are targets of this roadmap (Layer 1).

sourceIssues.printed: The tensor group of the generated crystalline representation category is identified with MT, although Definition 5.1 defines MT as the identity component of Zariski closure.
sourceIssues.correction: Use the full closure H for the neutral tensor group and its finite-field crystalline partner. Take H° only when applying the connected Mumford–Tate conclusion, or first restrict to a finite extension killing the finite component group.
sourceIssues.reason: The category of a finite nontrivial representation has a finite nontrivial tensor group, while its connected algebraic monodromy is trivial. Normal connected G_der can still be transferred by the ambient period comparison.
sourceIssues.known: Already recorded in PAPER-GLEASON-LIM-XU-26/E02 and PadicHodgeTheory/E53; checked here in the published paragraph. No published correction located in the listed search.
searched: arXiv:2208.07195 v3 read through the sources service on 2026-10-25; no correction located.

sourceIssues.printed: Refined highest-weight pieces are indexed using Gal(E/k) even when the reflex field E/k need not be normal; that notation does not enumerate all required refinements in the nonnormal case.
sourceIssues.correction: Use the threshold min_{λ∈O} ⟨w_0λ, μ⟩, equivalently the minimum over all Γ_E-orbits C ⊆ O of ⟨w_0 q_C, μ⟩; weight the refined orbits by |C|/|O| in averages.
sourceIssues.reason: Take k=Q_5, E=k(cube root of 5), G=Res_{E/k}G_m and V=E. The μ selecting the identity embedding has reflex field E with trivial automorphism group. The geometric weight orbit has three members, refining into orbits of sizes 1 and 2. Their μ-pairings are 1 and 0. The true generic filtration on V has jump 0; testing only the identity refinement can predict jump 1.
sourceIssues.known: The nonnormal-reflex problem is already recorded in PAPER-GLEASON-LIM-XU-26/E06. This package supplies the explicit orbit partition and arithmetic consumer; no published correction located.
searched: arXiv:2208.07195 v3 read through the sources service on 2026-10-25; no correction located.

sourceIssues.printed: The proof recovers an isotypic vector by summing its refined components over every reflex-field automorphism.
sourceIssues.correction: Sum once over distinct refined Γ_E-orbits C⊆O. In averages use the coefficient |C|/|O|.
sourceIssues.reason: Even if E/k is quadratic Galois, the trivial highest weight has only one refined piece. Summing it over both automorphisms gives 2v rather than v. The minimum in the degree argument is unchanged by duplicates, but the printed vector equality fails.
searched: arXiv:2208.07195 v3 read through the sources service on 2026-10-25; no correction located.

sourceIssues.printed: The reduction to a faithful representation asserts that every representation embeds into a single mixed tensor power of that representation.
sourceIssues.correction: Allow finite direct sums and subquotients of mixed tensor powers, and justify how line tests transport. This package uses Proposition 3.3.4(1) with all representations, so that reduction is unnecessary.
sourceIssues.reason: For G=G_m with its faithful weight-one representation, every single mixed tensor power has only one weight. The representation 1⊕χ has two distinct weights and cannot embed into one such power.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Lemma 6.12, arXiv v3 pp. 50–51, invoking Lemma 3.2
sourceIssues.printed: The proof uses an unrestricted component-of-quotient formula to descend a Galois orbit as a connected component.
sourceIssues.correction: For this application prove compactness of the Galois image, connectedness of each descended orbit through finite transitive covers, and invariant clopen separation of different compact cosets. The general quotient formula needs a separation hypothesis.
sourceIssues.reason: An arbitrary orbit quotient of a disconnected space can be connected; the previously recorded failure of Lemma 3.2 cannot justify this step. The compact Galois orbit has the stronger separation property needed here.
sourceIssues.known: The unrestricted quotient error is already recorded in PAPER-GLEASON-LIM-XU-26/E01 and repaired conditionally in DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/components-of-restricted-quotients. The compact application is proved separately here.
searched: arXiv:2208.07195 v3 read through the sources service on 2026-10-25; no correction located.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 6.7, crystalline step, arXiv v3 p. 47
sourceIssues.printed: The openness argument treats the Galois image as a subgroup of the derived group, whereas condition (4) concerns its intersection with that group.
sourceIssues.correction: Compare full algebraic monodromy, use central lifting of derived containment, and apply Serre–Sen to the crystalline lift. A finite central isogeny on derived groups alone does not compare the two intersections.
sourceIssues.reason: The Galois image of a crystalline representation can have a nontrivial central character, so it is not in general contained in G_tilde_der. The parent openness theorem supplies the missing bridge once derived containment is proved.
searched: arXiv:2208.07195 v3 read through the sources service on 2026-10-25; no correction located.

sourceIssues.locator: Justification of equation (5.34), arXiv v3 p. 39
sourceIssues.printed: The text explains moving the Frobenius action across the pairing with the same positive exponent.
sourceIssues.correction: Equivariance first moves it with the inverse exponent. The displayed full-period sum remains correct by reindexing all s powers, using σ_0^s=1.
sourceIssues.reason: For an invariant pairing, ⟨σ^iλ,μ⟩=⟨λ,σ^(-i)μ⟩. The positive and inverse sums agree over a whole period, but the termwise justification has the wrong action direction.
searched: arXiv:2208.07195 v3 read through the sources service on 2026-10-25; no correction located.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 2.0.3 proof, choice of b and last residue-degree inequality, p. 735
sourceIssues.printed: The explicitly imposed growth bound has factor m p^{b(m−1)}, while the degree at n=bm+r used at the end is m p^{n−b}=m p^{b(m−1)+r}.
sourceIssues.correction: Choose b sufficiently large for the stronger residue-degree bound N>M m p^{b(m−1)+r}. The same factorial growth limits permit this, with fixed r.
sourceIssues.reason: The leading-digit lemma has degree m p^{n−b}, so for r>0 the stated earlier bound lacks the factor p^r required for the final no-root argument. Strengthening the choice of b repairs the proof and leaves infinite transcendence unchanged.
sourceIssues.affects: the proof (the transcendence statement is owned by ReductiveGroupsPartII §RG2.0.4)
